result.summary: Read core-directives.md and security-invariants.md (all S1-S14) in full, then docs/agents/design/REQ-025.md and REQ-025-schema.md in full, then read the actual diff myself (git diff master...HEAD) rather than trusting BACKEND-DEV's or REVIEWER's reports: apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts (full, byte by byte), apps/bot/src/scheduler/rateLimiter.ts (full), apps/bot/src/scheduler/runner.ts (full), apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts (full diff), apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts diff, apps/bot/src/index.ts diff, apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts's notificationLedger block, apps/bot/drizzle/0005_violet_venom.sql (full). S9 PRIMARY FOCUS -- own adversarial concurrent-call race, beyond REVIEWER's sequential two-process kill test: REVIEWER's own AC1 test proved sequential restart-idempotency (process 1 completes and exits, then process 2 runs). My own scenario was different and specifically targeted the task's stated concern: TWO GENUINELY CONCURRENT calls to sendLedgeredNotification for the identical (registrationId, kind), both in flight AT THE SAME TIME, to rule out a race window where both could pass an earlier check before the INSERT. I traced sendLedgeredNotification's exact sequencing first (domain/notification.ts lines ~78-128): step 1 resolves the user (no registration/kind involved), step 2 checks user.blocked (no registration/kind involved), step 3 checks broadcastOptIn for marketing only (no registration/kind involved) -- NONE of steps 1-3 reads or checks anything keyed on (registrationId, kind). The FIRST and ONLY place (registrationId, kind) is touched at all is step 4's `db.insert(notificationLedger).values({registrationId, kind})`. This means there is structurally no earlier check for two concurrent calls to race past -- the INSERT itself, arbitrated by Postgres's own UNIQUE index (uq_notification_ledger_registration_kind) via its btree page lock, is the only serialization point, and it is atomic by construction (not a read-then-write pattern like S7's capacity concern). I did not accept this as merely 'looks correct by inspection' and instead ran it for real, twice, at two different concurrency granularities: (1) Same process, same connection pool, launched via Promise.all with a sender that sleeps 50ms mid-send to guarantee genuine overlap -- result: {sent} + {skipped-already-sent}, sendCount=1, ledgerRowCount=1. (2) Two FULLY SEPARATE `pg.Pool` instances (two independent DB sessions/sockets, not one pool queueing internally), launched via Promise.all with an 80ms mid-send sleep -- result: {sent} + {skipped-already-sent}, sendCount=1, ledgerRowCount=1, reproduced identically across 5 repeated trials with fresh fixtures each time (no flakiness observed). Both constructions used a throwaway scratch script (apps/bot/.secreview-scratch/, written, run, and deleted after use -- not committed; git status --short confirmed clean afterward) seeding a fresh chapter/user/venue/event/admitted-registration via drizzle directly against the scratch Postgres (bot-postgres-1, already migrated to 0005). This independently confirms the DB UNIQUE constraint genuinely serializes true concurrency, not just sequential restarts: there is no window, at any granularity I could construct, where two concurrent calls both proceed past an idempotency check before the ledger write -- because no such earlier check exists to race past in the first place. Also confirmed no in-memory tracker exists anywhere that a restart or a second process would lose (grep for `new Set|new Map|WeakMap` across notification.ts/scheduler/*.ts/withdraw.ts -- no match, matching REVIEWER's own grep). S10 -- re-derived the truth table myself against the exact security-invariants.md S10 wording, cell by cell, by reading domain/notification.ts's step 2/3 ordering directly (not from the design doc's prose): - transactional + not-blocked -> sent: step 2 (blocked=false, passes) -> step 3 skipped entirely for transactional (classification check is `if (classification === 'marketing')`) -> proceeds to insert+send. CORRECT. - transactional + blocked -> skip: step 2 returns `skipped-blocked` unconditionally, before any classification branch. CORRECT -- and confirms the invariant's specific requirement that blocked is checked 'before the classification branch', not as a a two-key lookup that a marketing-only gate could accidentally miss. - marketing + opted-in + not-blocked -> sent: step 2 passes, step 3's `!user.broadcastOptIn` is false (opted in) so proceeds, insert+send. CORRECT. - marketing + opted-out -> skip: step 3 returns `skipped-no-broadcast-opt-in` for a non-blocked, opted-out user on a marketing call. CORRECT. - marketing + blocked -> skip: step 2 returns `skipped-blocked` before step 3 is ever reached, regardless of broadcastOptIn's value. CORRECT. All five cells match exactly. Note: Release 1's own `NotificationKind` union (admission_result, waitlist_promotion, reminder_24h, reminder_3h, feedback_request, event_cancelled) is entirely transactional per S10's own classification table, and the one production call site (withdraw.ts's sendPromotionNotification) hardcodes `classification: 'transactional'` -- so cells 3-5 of the table above are exercised only by my own direct test of sendLedgeredNotification, not by any reachable production code path yet. This is a correctly scoped Release 1 (marketing kinds are named in the design as Release 3 future work) and not a gap: the marketing branch's CODE exists and is correct today even though nothing currently calls it with classification:'marketing', so there is no live marketing send this diff could misclassify. The '2 per user per week' marketing cap named in S10 is therefore also correctly N/A for this diff -- no marketing send exists yet to cap. New authorization/exposure concerns (own investigation, not in REVIEWER's scope): sendLedgeredNotification itself performs NO caller-identity/ownership check and accepts a bare registrationId/userId. Traced whether this is a gap: its only production call site is withdraw.ts's sendPromotionNotification, called from makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler only after `outcome.promotion.kind === 'promoted'` -- and outcome.promotion.registrationId/promotedUserId are NOT attacker-controlled Telegram input, they are values computed server-side inside registration.ts's `promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible` (called from within the same DB transaction as the withdrawal, selecting the next eligible waitlisted registration internally -- confirmed by reading registration.ts lines ~499-564: the promoted registration/user come from a query over the event's own waitlist, never from ctx.callbackQuery data). So sendLedgeredNotification correctly relies on its caller's authorization context rather than needing its own -- it is an internal domain function, not a handler, and has no Telegram-facing route that lets a user directly choose an arbitrary (registrationId, kind, userId) triple. This is the correct shape for an internal API and not a defect, but I flag it as worth documenting explicitly in the design doc for future call sites (REQ-026/027's reminder/cancellation jobs): any FUTURE caller of sendLedgeredNotification must itself supply only server-derived ids, never raw user input, since this function performs no ownership check of its own. Filed as an issue-queue item below (MINOR, forward-looking, not a defect in this diff). Ledger content exposure: grepped the full apps/bot/src tree for notificationLedger/notification_ledger usage -- appears only in domain/notification.ts (the insert) and db/schema.ts (the table definition). No handler, export, or query anywhere reads back ledger rows to any Telegram-facing surface. A user cannot query their own or anyone else's notification history through any reachable code path in this diff. S3/S12 not implicated. Rate limiter / scheduler DoS-adjacent concern: traced whether a malicious high-volume trigger of the ledger-check-then-send path could exhaust Telegram's API quota for legitimate messages. `createRateLimitedSender` wraps every send through one process-wide `RollingWindowPacer` (25 msg/s, matching Telegram's actual global rate limit) shared across ALL callers via the single `notificationSender` instance constructed once in index.ts and threaded through every handler -- confirmed index.ts's diff constructs exactly one instance and passes it to `makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler`, with the comment noting future REQ-026/027 call sites will reuse the same instance. Because the pacer is shared process-wide (not per-caller, per-user, or per-job), one caller triggering many sends is throttled by the SAME global window that governs every other caller -- messages queue and wait for a slot rather than being dropped or exceeding Telegram's own limit, so this design cannot cause Telegram to rate-limit or ban the bot's token regardless of trigger volume. The only currently reachable trigger of a ledgered send (withdraw -> promotion) is gated by the same registration/withdraw authorization already reviewed under REQ-020/022/023's own gates -- it is not a bare unauthenticated endpoint, so there is no new unauthenticated-flood vector introduced by this diff. No DoS-adjacent gap found for what is actually reachable today. S13 migration sign-off: read apps/bot/drizzle/0005_violet_venom.sql directly, not a description of it. It contains exactly one CREATE TABLE (new notification_ledger table only, no ALTER/DROP/RENAME of any existing table or column), one FK ALTER (ON DELETE RESTRICT, protecting registrations from being deleted out from under a ledger row -- correct direction, prevents data loss rather than causing it), and one CREATE UNIQUE INDEX. Nothing here drops, renames, or rewrites a column or table holding personal data or attendance history -- S13's mandatory-sign-off trigger condition is not met by this migration, matching REVIEWER's own conclusion, independently re-confirmed by me reading the raw SQL rather than trusting that conclusion. Remaining S1-S14 items, each re-derived against this diff specifically: - S1 (consent precedes storage): N/A -- no User/Profile consent-column writes in this diff; confirmed by reading the full notification.ts/rateLimiter.ts/runner.ts (no insert/update touching consent_pd_at/broadcast_opt_in/publish_consent; broadcastOptIn is only ever READ, never written, by this diff). - S2 (authorization on the action, negative path proven): applies indirectly -- sendLedgeredNotification is an internal function with no user-facing route of its own; its one call site is gated by the already-reviewed withdraw/promotion authorization chain (REQ-020/022/023), and the promoted registration/user ids are server-derived, not attacker-suppliable (traced above). No new authorization surface introduced. - S3 (member reads only own Profile): N/A for new reads -- sendLedgeredNotification reads only the acting-context's already-authorized user row via getUserForNotificationById (unchanged read shape, one new column: broadcastOptIn); confirmed no ledger-content exposure to any handler (grepped, see above). - S4 (tokens unguessable): N/A -- no token generation in this diff; qrToken passed into the promotion notification's composed text is the pre-existing REQ-020/023 token, unchanged here, read-only. - S5/S6/S7 (check-in refusal/audit, checked_in_at gating, capacity+override audit): N/A -- no check-in or capacity code touched; confirmed handlers/checkin.ts absent from `git diff --name-only master...HEAD`. - S8 (exactly one AuditLog row per status change): N/A for this diff's own writes -- notification_ledger is not an AuditLog row and this diff's only status-changing write path (withdrawRegistration -> promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible) is unchanged code, already gated at REQ-022/023's own reviews; confirmed the notification send happens strictly after that transaction has already committed (withdraw.ts calls sendPromotionNotification after the `db.transaction(...)` call returns), so a notification failure cannot roll back or duplicate the audit write. - S9: PASS -- see primary-focus section above. Own concurrent-call race constructed and run twice at two concurrency granularities, 6 total trials, zero flakiness; DB UNIQUE constraint is the entire mechanism, confirmed atomic by construction (no earlier check to race past) and by direct experiment. - S10: PASS -- full 5-cell truth table re-derived from the code and verified to match S10's exact wording; marketing/cap cells correctly unreachable-but-correctly-coded in this Release-1-scoped diff. - S11 (PII never in plaintext logs): grepped domain/notification.ts, scheduler/rateLimiter.ts, scheduler/runner.ts for any `console.`/logger call -- only runner.ts's one `log.error('scheduled job failed', { job: job.name, error: err })`, which logs a job NAME (a static string like 'reminder-24h-job', not user data) and an error object; no job is registered yet (`startScheduledJobs([])`) so this call path is unreachable in this diff, and even when reached in a future requirement, `err` here is a job-runner-level failure (e.g. a DB connection error), not a per-message payload -- flagged as worth re-checking under S11 specifically when REQ-026/027 populate real jobs whose `run()` bodies may throw errors containing PII-bearing objects, since a bare `error: err` shape would surface whatever an underlying rejection carries. Not a defect in THIS diff (no reachable path logs PII today), but forwarded as a forward-looking note, not silently dropped. - S12 (exports role-gated/audited): N/A -- no export functionality in this diff. - S13: PASS -- see migration sign-off above. Purely additive, no PII column touched, sign-off trigger not met. - S14 (publication consent default-off): N/A -- no Profile/publish_consent code touched. COMMANDS RUN BY ME, REAL OUTPUT: `npm run lint` (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors, 2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings (unchanged by this diff). `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces clean (Next.js build succeeded; apps/bot's tsc clean). `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root) -> 19 files / 217 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- matches BACKEND-DEV's and REVIEWER's reported count, independently re-run by me a third time. Scope/hygiene check: `git status --short` clean before this handoff's own commit -- my own scratch verification directory (apps/bot/.secreview-scratch/) was deleted immediately after use, and the scratch Postgres was truncated back to empty after my own seeded fixtures (chapters/users/venues/events/registrations/notification_ledger rows) to avoid leaving test data behind for the next agent's own DB-backed suite runs. Verdict: PASS. S9 and S10 -- this requirement's own named purpose -- both independently re-derived and re-verified with my own adversarial constructions distinct from REVIEWER's (a true-concurrency race at two connection granularities for S9; a full re-derivation of the 5-cell truth table directly from the code for S10). No new authorization/exposure gap found; the one forward-looking note (sendLedgeredNotification's callers must supply only server-derived ids; S11 log-shape risk once real jobs are added) is filed as guidance for REQ-026/027, not a blocking defect in this diff.

evidence.s9_concurrent_race_result: CONFIRMED SAFE at two concurrency granularities beyond REVIEWER's sequential two-process test: a same-pool Promise.all race and a two-independent-pg.Pool race for the identical (registrationId, kind), both with an artificial mid-send delay to force genuine overlap. Both produced exactly one 'sent', one 'skipped-already-sent', sendCount=1, ledgerRowCount=1, reproduced across 6 total trials with 0 flakiness. Root cause confirmed by code trace: no check in sendLedgeredNotification reads or branches on (registrationId, kind) before the single atomic INSERT, so there is no earlier check for two concurrent calls to race past -- the Postgres UNIQUE index is the sole and sufficient serialization mechanism.
evidence.s10_truth_table_verification: All 5 cells (transactional+not-blocked=sent, transactional+blocked=skip, marketing+opted-in+not-blocked=sent, marketing+opted-out=skip, marketing+blocked=skip) verified directly against domain/notification.ts's step 2 (unconditional blocked check, precedes classification branch) and step 3 (classification-gated broadcastOptIn check) code. evidence.authorization_scope_check: sendLedgeredNotification performs no ownership check of its own; traced its one call site (withdraw.ts's sendPromotionNotification) to confirm the registrationId/userId it receives are server-derived from promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible's own waitlist query inside the same DB transaction, never from attacker-controlled Telegram update data. Correctly relies on caller authorization -- flagged as guidance (not a defect) for future callers in REQ-026/027 to preserve this property.

evidence.rate_limiter_dos_check: One process-wide RollingWindowPacer instance (25 msg/s) shared across all current and future callers via a single notificationSender constructed once in index.ts -- throttling is global, not per-caller, so no caller can exceed or starve Telegram's actual rate limit for others. issues.title: sendLedgeredNotification has no ownership check of its own -- document the caller-contract for future call sites
issues.description: domain/notification.ts's sendLedgeredNotification accepts a bare registrationId/userId with no verification that they belong together or that the caller is authorized to notify that user. This is correct and safe today because its only call site (withdraw.ts's sendPromotionNotification) supplies server-derived ids from promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible's own internal waitlist query, never from raw Telegram update data. REQ-026 (reminders) and REQ-027 (cancellation notices) will add new call sites -- CODE-DESIGNER/BACKEND-DEV for those requirements should explicitly re-confirm each new caller supplies only server-derived ids, since sendLedgeredNotification itself will not catch a caller that passes user-influenced input. Recommend a one-line callout in REQ-025.md's own docs or a shared caller-contract note, not a code change to this diff.

issues.title: runner.ts's failure log uses a bare `error: err` shape -- revisit for S11 once real jobs exist
issues.description: scheduler/runner.ts's `log.error('scheduled job failed', { job: job.name, error: err })` is unreachable in this diff (no job is registered: startScheduledJobs([])) and today would only ever log a job-runner-level failure (e.g. a DB connectivity error), not per-message PII. Once REQ-026/027 register real jobs whose run() bodies may reject with an error object that happens to carry a user profile/phone/email (e.g. a thrown error from deep inside a per-user loop), this log call would surface it in plaintext, violating S11. Not a defect in this diff since no such job exists yet -- flagged so SECURITY-REVIEWER's next gate on REQ-026/027 checks whether any job's error path can leak PII into this log call.
